newsitem.title: USA: Western Atlas to acquire Norand.
newsitem.headline: Western Atlas to acquire Norand.

text.p: Western Atlas Inc. has agreed to acquire Norand Corp., a developer of mobile computing systems and wireless data communications networks, for $261.3 million in cash, the companies said Wednesday.
Under the definitive agreement, Western Atlas will offer $33.50 a share for all 7.8 million shares of Norand common stock outstanding through a cash tender offer.
Norand's stock shot up $13.375 to $32.75 early on Nasdaq. Western Atlas edged down 25 cents to $71.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The offer, which has been unanimously approved by both companies' boards, is subject to approval by Norand stockholders and antitrust regulators.

"This acquisition will establish Western Atlas -- through its Intermec division -- as the company with the broadest technology range and most extensive distribution network in the industrial automated data collection and mobile computing solutions industries," said Alton J. Brann, chairman of Western Atlas.
"This is a combination of two companies with complementary technologies, distribution channels and application know-how."
Western Atlas, based in Beverly Hills, Calif., is a global supplier of oilfield information services and industrial automation systems with annual revenues of more than $2.5 billion.
Norand, based in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, designs, manufactures and markets mobile computing systems and wireless data communications networks using radio frequency technology.
